stories.head: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire as attacks continue
stories.say: Donald Trump says Russia and Ukraine agreed to stop hitting energy sites. Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it news to him, and said a Kharkiv power plant was struck on Sunday evening.
stories.stand: The US president gave no terms, the Kremlin did not immediately respond, and Kyiv said Russian strikes on energy sites went on.
body: Donald Trump said on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed an "energy ceasefire" taking effect immediately. In a social media post he said both sides had agreed, but he gave no details of the terms.

Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Axios the announcement was news to him. He said Ukraine was ready to stop striking Russian energy sites if Russia did the same. He reported drone and glide bomb attacks during the day and a strike on a power plant in Kharkiv in the evening.
The Kremlin did not immediately comment. Trump made a similar announcement in mid-September that neither side confirmed.
The post followed Trump's call on Saturday for Ukraine to get a new president. Zelenskyy replied that Ukraine could organise elections after a 60-day total ceasefire.

stories.head: Riyadh airport hit again and kept shut after deadly Houthi strike
stories.say: Riyadh's main airport was struck again on Sunday and stayed shut, a day after an attack killed twelve people. The Houthis have told travellers to avoid Saudi airports.
stories.stand: A terminal at King Khalid International Airport was struck on Sunday as the Houthis threatened all Saudi airports except those in Mecca and Medina.
body: A passenger terminal at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport was struck on Sunday, Saudi authorities said. It came a day after a Houthi attack killed 12 people and injured more than 300.
India's embassy said an Indian national wounded on Saturday died on Sunday. The airport stayed closed on Sunday and Riyadh schools moved to online lessons.
The Houthis said they had carried out four operations in 24 hours. They told airlines and travellers to avoid Saudi airports and airspace, except in Mecca and Medina.
Donald Trump said on Saturday the US may join Saudi strikes on the Houthis. Several airlines, including Lufthansa Group and Emirates, suspended Riyadh flights.

stories.head: At least 139 dead after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti
stories.say: At least one hundred and thirty-nine people, fifteen of them children, died when a migrant boat bound for Yemen capsized off Djibouti, the UN said. Eighty-four are missing.
stories.stand: The UN migration agency says the boat was carrying about 300 people from Djibouti towards Yemen when it sank near Guhere.
body: A boat carrying about 300 migrants capsized off Djibouti's eastern coast near Guhere, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Sunday. It was heading for Yemen.
At least 139 people died, including 15 children, and 84 are missing. More than 80 survived, all of them Ethiopian nationals. The toll rose from 109 after more bodies were recovered.
The IOM's head of mission in Djibouti, Alexandre Coissac, called it "a devastating loss of life". Search and rescue work was continuing.
The route across the Bab al-Mandeb strait is used by migrants from the Horn of Africa seeking work in Gulf countries.

stories.head: Pope Leo to have surgery to remove lung nodule
stories.say: Pope Leo says he will have surgery in the coming days to remove a nodule found in his lung. He said on Sunday it was caught early, and the Vatican expects a week's recovery.
stories.stand: The 71-year-old pontiff disclosed the finding at his Sunday Angelus, saying doctors had advised an operation.
body: Pope Leo XIV told crowds in St Peter's Square on Sunday that recent medical checks had found a localised nodule in his lung. He said it was found early and that doctors had advised removing it.
He said the operation was scheduled for the coming days and asked for prayers. The Vatican said recovery should take about a week.
The Vatican has not said whether the nodule is malignant. Leo, 71, has no previously known health problems.
He is due to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November.

stories.head: Pakistan imposes emergency rule in Imran Khan party's province
stories.say: Pakistan has suspended the government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, run by Imran Khan's party, saying it stepped back from fighting terrorism. Its chief minister has reportedly been arrested.
stories.stand: The federal government suspended the PTI-run government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday, citing its record on fighting militancy.
body: Pakistan's federal government imposed emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday. President Asif Ali Zardari approved a cabinet recommendation made under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

The move suspends the provincial government run by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan. The prime minister's office accused it of deliberately disengaging from the fight against terrorism.
PTI figures said Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and the party's provincial president had been arrested. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said the emergency would initially last six months.
A PTI spokesman called it a coup disguised as an emergency. PTI had been planning a march on Islamabad to demand Khan's release.

stories.head: Hurricane Simon lashes Mexico's Pacific coast
stories.say: Hurricane Simon churned along Mexico's Pacific coast on Sunday night. President Claudia Sheinbaum urged people in four states to stay sheltered as forecasters warned of flooding.
stories.stand: Forecasters warned of dangerous wind, storm surge and up to 30 inches of rain as the storm tracked near Jalisco.
body: Hurricane Simon moved along Mexico's west-central coast on Sunday after strengthening to Category 4 on Saturday. The US National Hurricane Center said Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco faced the greatest risk of a direct hit.
Forecasters warned of life-threatening storm surge, flooding and mudslides. Up to 30 inches of rain was possible in parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco.
President Claudia Sheinbaum urged people in Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacan to stay sheltered. Classes were suspended and evacuations were under way. No casualties had been reported on Sunday.

stories.say: A landslide blocked a river in Nepal's Gorkha district on Sunday, unleashing a flash flood that swept away homes and bridges. Five people are out of contact.

body: A landslide blocked the Budhi Gandaki river in Nepal's Gorkha district on Sunday, triggering a flash flood downstream. About a dozen houses and two suspension bridges were swept away.
Nepal's disaster authority said five people were out of contact. No deaths had been reported. The army said it rescued 49 people.
Officials told villagers along the river in five districts to move to safer areas. The river feeds the Trishuli, where a glacier collapse caused deadly floods in August.

stories.say: A man has died after entering the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Saturday. Police say the tiger was unhurt, and the park says it will not be put down.

body: A man died on Saturday afternoon after entering the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster. South Yorkshire Police said they were called at 1.35pm and the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

Police said the tiger attacked the man, causing serious injuries. The animal was not hurt and stayed in its enclosure, and officers said there was no wider risk to the public. The man has not been publicly named.

The park was evacuated and stayed closed on Sunday. It said the tiger, an Amur tiger called Altai, is well and will not be put down. Police asked people not to share videos of the incident circulating online.
Yorkshire Ambulance Service sent two ambulances, an air ambulance and a doctor. Doncaster North MP Ed Miliband said he was deeply saddened.

stories.say: Police made at least twenty arrests as thousands marched for Palestine in central London on Saturday. Six people were held after climbing onto the Battle of Britain memorial.
stories.stand: The Metropolitan Police made at least 20 arrests during Saturday's march, including six people who climbed onto the Battle of Britain memorial.
body: Thousands of pro-Palestine protesters marched through central London on Saturday, days after the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks. The Metropolitan Police said it made at least 20 arrests.

Six people were held on suspicion of criminal damage after climbing onto the Battle of Britain memorial on Victoria Embankment. Two were arrested over placards supporting Palestine Action, which is banned as a terrorist group.

Police set conditions on the route and timing of the march, organised by the Palestine Coalition. A counter-protest of about 30 people gathered outside New Scotland Yard, with barriers keeping the groups apart.
Officers had powers to require people to remove face coverings. Deputy Assistant Commissioner Carl Galvin said the police presence would be significant.

stories.stand: Scotland's tertiary education minister has written to institutions about the risk of spying on campus, following an MI5 alert over a Chinese research body.
body: The Scottish Government has written to universities warning them to be aware of the risk of espionage on campus. The letter follows an MI5 alert in late September about the China General Technology Research Institute.
MI5 said the institute's main purpose is funding research that boosts the spying capabilities of China's Ministry of State Security. It strongly advised academics to review any links with it.

Tertiary education minister Alyn Smith said the government takes the alert seriously and is working with the UK Government and the Scottish Funding Council. He said confidential reporting routes exist for worried academics.
Edinburgh and St Andrews universities said they have no links to the institute, according to The Scotsman. The Chinese Embassy in London called the accusation fabricated.

Chief Inspector Cherith Craig called it a reckless attack in a built-up residential area, saying it could have seriously injured officers or residents. Police have opened an investigation and appealed for information.

body: Nigel Farage is due to announce on Monday that a Reform UK government would suspend asylum for a full parliamentary term of five years. Applications in progress would be declared void.

The party says it would scrap asylum tribunals, legal refugee routes and resettlement schemes. Roughly 90,000 outstanding asylum and protection appeals would not be heard, and the claimants would be deported.
Reform also says it would use tariffs and airline bans against countries that refuse to take back migrants. Farage told The Telegraph the country faces a national security emergency.
Labour called the plans a sign of desperation. Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said they largely copy Conservative policy.

body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says officials told him Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit referendum. He said he asked the question after entering Downing Street in July and was given a clear yes.
Burnham made the remarks on The Rest Is Politics podcast, with the episode due out on Monday. He has not set out how Russia interfered or what evidence the assessment rests on.

He said he wanted the issue on record to help voters in Germany and France see that some politics is driven by hostile states. He said German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told him the far-right AfD is linked to Russia.

In 2020, Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee found the government had not fully assessed Russian influence on the referendum. Russia has long said it does not meddle in other countries' votes.

It follows a vote at the party conference in Brighton in which members passed a motion defining Zionism as racism. Four of the party's five MPs rejected the motion.

Polanski did not vote, having left to campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, which Labour won. He said some members felt let down, and that he agreed with the motion's broad substance but not all of it.
Green MP Ellie Chowns said the party must not be vulnerable to capture by extremists. Israel barred Polanski from entering the country after the vote.

stories.stand: The annual meetings run from 12 to 18 October, the first held outside Washington in three years.
body: The International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings run in Bangkok from 12 to 18 October. It is the first time in three years they have been held outside Washington.
The Iran war, now in its eighth month, and its effect on energy prices and inflation are expected to dominate. The IMF expects global growth of about 3% this year.
Global public debt is at its highest since the Second World War and is projected to pass 100% of GDP by 2030, according to the IMF.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is skipping the meetings, citing domestic commitments. Two senior Treasury officials will lead the US delegation instead.

stories.head: World's timekeepers meet to decide whether to scrap the leap second
stories.say: Delegates meeting near Versailles from Monday are expected to vote on retiring the leap second, letting clock time drift from Earth's rotation until a leap hour is needed.
stories.stand: A proposal before the international weights and measures conference would end the extra seconds added to clocks since 1972.
body: The governing body of the International Bureau of Weights and Measures meets near Versailles, in France, from 12 to 15 October. A vote on the leap second is expected during the meeting.

The leading proposal would let Coordinated Universal Time drift away from Earth's rotation until the gap reaches an hour. A leap hour would then be added. New Atlas reports that, if adopted, the change would apply from 20 May 2027.
Leap seconds have been added 27 times since 1972, most recently in 2016. They have caused software failures at platforms including Cloudflare and Reddit, ABC News reports.

Michael Wouters of Australia's National Measurement Institute told ABC there were no clear economic or practical arguments for keeping them. Earth's recent speeding up had raised the prospect of an untested negative leap second.

body: Philippe Sands, the British-French international lawyer and author, received the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade at Frankfurt's Paulskirche on Sunday. The ceremony closed this year's Frankfurt Book Fair.

The prize, worth 25,000 euros, honours his work for justice, peace and the defence of international law, according to reports. German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier attended. Mirjam Zadoff, director of the Munich Documentation Centre for the History of National Socialism, gave the tribute.

In his speech, Sands accused Germany of staying silent about Israel, Gaza and the West Bank. He said criticising breaches of international law was not antisemitic. He condemned the Hamas attacks of 7 October 2023 and said Israel's right to self-defence was limited by international law.

stories.head: Frankfurt Book Fair closes with 236,000 visitors
stories.say: The Frankfurt Book Fair ended on Sunday after drawing two hundred and thirty-six thousand visitors, organisers said, with Czechia as guest of honour and Chile named for next year.
stories.stand: Organisers say attendance at the world's biggest book fair held steady, with Czechia as guest of honour and Chile named for 2027.
body: The 78th Frankfurt Book Fair ended on Sunday after five days. Organisers said it drew 236,000 visitors, split almost evenly between trade and public visitors.

According to the fair, 4,000 exhibitors from 137 countries took part. More than 3,800 events were held at the fairground and around the city. Organisers said attendance was at about the same level as last year.

Czechia was guest of honour, bringing 75 authors under the theme 'A Country on the Coast'. The Czech pavilion's events with writers such as Jáchym Topol and Radka Denemarková drew large audiences, a Czech outlet reported.
The next fair will run from 6 to 10 October 2027, with Chile as guest of honour, the organisers said.

body: Other Mommy, a horror film starring Jessica Chastain, took an estimated $27.5m in North America over the weekend. Industry estimates were released on Sunday.
The Universal and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster film had a reported budget of $19m, TheWrap reported. It received a D+ grade from audiences polled by CinemaScore.
The Social Reckoning, Aaron Sorkin's sequel to The Social Network, opened in fifth place with $5.5m. Second-weekend thriller Verity came second, and Resident Evil was third with $8.3m.

stories.head: Art Garfunkel postpones UK tour dates with respiratory infection
stories.say: Art Garfunkel has postponed his UK concerts in Watford, Manchester, Wolverhampton and London after a respiratory infection. The eighty-four-year-old says his heart is broken.
stories.stand: The 84-year-old singer said doctors advised rest after diagnosing the infection during rehearsals; ticket holders are told to keep their tickets.
body: Art Garfunkel has postponed the UK leg of his What A Wonderful World tour after being diagnosed with a respiratory infection. The 84-year-old said his doctor had advised rest.
The postponed shows were due in Watford, Manchester, Wolverhampton and London's Royal Albert Hall between 13 and 19 October, NME reported. No new dates have yet been set.
Ticket holders have been told to keep their tickets, which will be valid for the rescheduled shows. Garfunkel said he would return to the stage as soon as his health allowed.

body: The Raconteurs reunited on stage on Saturday night for the first time since 2019. They joined Jack White for the encore of his Nashville concert.
White, Brendan Benson, Jack Lawrence and Patrick Keeler played five songs at The Truth, a new venue in the city. They included Steady, As She Goes and Carolina Drama.
The band's last album, Help Us Stranger, came out in 2019. White released his seventh solo album, Frozen Charlotte, in July and has been touring this year, NME reported.

stories.head: Archaeologists uncover 300-metre stretch of ancient Jerusalem aqueduct
stories.say: Israeli archaeologists have uncovered a three-hundred-metre stretch of Jerusalem's Lower Aqueduct, which they believe dates back around two thousand years to the Hasmonean period.
stories.stand: The Israel Antiquities Authority says the section, found before planned building work, will be preserved as a public park.
body: The Israel Antiquities Authority (IAA) said on Sunday it had uncovered a 300-metre section of Jerusalem's Lower Aqueduct, south of the city centre.

Archaeologists believe the aqueduct was built in the Hasmonean period, about 2,000 years ago. It carried water by gravity for more than 20 kilometres from Solomon's Pools, south of Bethlehem, to Jerusalem.

The excavation was carried out ahead of construction of a planned new neighbourhood. The IAA and the Israel Land Authority say the section will be preserved and opened to the public as part of the development.
Ceramic pipes were fitted inside the channel about 500 years ago, during the Ottoman period. The excavators said it stayed in use until about a century ago.

stories.head: Verstappen wins Singapore Grand Prix for the first time
stories.say: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix from pole on Sunday, his first win at Marina Bay, ahead of Charles Leclerc and championship leader Kimi Antonelli.
stories.stand: The Red Bull driver led every lap from pole in his 250th race, with Leclerc second and Antonelli third.
body: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix on Sunday, leading every lap from pole position. It was his first win at Marina Bay and came in his 250th Grand Prix start.
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished 7.3 seconds behind in second. Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli was third, with McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri fourth and fifth.
Lewis Hamilton, who stayed out on a one-stop strategy, dropped to sixth and apologised to his team over the radio. George Russell recovered from 19th on the grid to finish ninth.
Antonelli now leads the drivers' standings by 102 points from Russell, according to Sports Illustrated. The next race is the United States Grand Prix in Austin from 23 to 25 October.

stories.head: Manchester City beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield
stories.say: Manchester City won three-nil at ten-man Liverpool on Sunday, scoring three times after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off, to go three points clear at the top of the Premier League.

body: Manchester City beat Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday. All three goals came after Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for a second yellow card.
Gravenberch was dismissed in the 62nd minute for a foul on Jeremy Doku, Goal reported. Erling Haaland scored about three minutes later, Doku added a second soon after and Rayan Cherki made it three.
The win restores City's three-point lead at the top of the Premier League table. NBC Sports reported they have won all six league games this season.
Al Jazeera reported it was City's first match since an independent commission found the club guilty of over 100 breaches of financial rules. No sanction has yet been announced.

stories.head: All Blacks beat Wallabies 50-19 to keep Bledisloe Cup
stories.say: New Zealand beat Australia fifty points to nineteen at Eden Park on Saturday, scoring seven tries to keep the Bledisloe Cup and stretch their unbeaten home run against the Wallabies.
stories.stand: New Zealand scored seven tries to three at Eden Park, where Australia have not won for 40 years.
body: New Zealand beat Australia 50-19 at Eden Park in Auckland on Saturday to retain the Bledisloe Cup. The All Blacks led only 17-14 at half-time before pulling away.
The hosts scored seven tries to Australia's three, ABC News reported, with Damian McKenzie kicking six conversions and a penalty. Will Jordan and Codie Taylor were among the try scorers.
ABC reported that New Zealand have now won 12 Tests in a row against Australia. The Wallabies have not won at Eden Park for 40 years. The sides meet again in Sydney next Saturday.

stories.say: Australia bowled South Africa out for two hundred and eighty-four on Sunday in the first Test in Durban, and closed on thirty-three without loss, a lead of one hundred and thirty-nine.
stories.stand: South Africa were bowled out 106 runs behind, and Australia reached 33 without loss before bad light ended play.
body: Australia took a firm hold on the first Test at Kingsmead on Sunday, bowling South Africa out for 284 in reply to their 390.
David Bedingham made 49 and Aiden Markram 37, while Tristan Stubbs and Wiaan Mulder added 32 and 30. Captain Pat Cummins was among the wicket-takers.
Australia reached 33 without loss in their second innings before bad light stopped play, giving them a lead of 139. Nic Maddinson was 17 not out and Travis Head 10.
Steve Smith took three slip catches, which Scrolla reported made him the leading outfield catcher in Test history. Day four begins on Monday.

stories.stand: The top seed beat Quentin Halys in three sets and next faces Alexander Bublik, as he chases the year-end No. 1 ranking.
body: Top seed Alexander Zverev beat France's Quentin Halys 6-4, 6-7, 6-3 at the Shanghai Masters on Sunday to reach the last 16.
It was the German's 60th tour-level win of 2026, the most of any player this season. He will next play 19th seed Alexander Bublik, who beat Brandon Nakashima.
World No. 1 Jannik Sinner has ended his season with a knee injury. The ATP says Zverev would secure the year-end No. 1 ranking by reaching the Shanghai semi-finals.
